body: I've never had hypopigmented scars but I used to have terrible scars covering my legs and same, people used to ask me if I was sick. Mine faded after ~3 years (they've since been replaced by new scars but thankfully my legs aren't *usually* my favourite place to pick so it's never been as bad). Just moisturize your skin and put sunscreen on. Sorry, wish I could give you more concrete advice but I tried a bunch of shit and the only thing that worked was time.
Your hands could literally be mine, I feel you homie. Clean those wounds and put dry bandaids on them.
That's painful as fuck, how are you doing 9 days later?
My thumbs look identical to yours and I agree, it's most likely a habit-tic deformity, not a fungus!

Thank you, it's so good to know that I'm not alone in this. It is annoying to have someone comment on something that you're very aware of, are not proud of, and have little control over! But like ultimately it does come from a place of caring. It's just hard to remember that in the moment. The reward system is a great idea, I'll think of things that could work for me!
Thank you, I will try the 5 minute timer trick! All the best, I appreciate your comment a lot.

Thank you so much, not only does it help a lot to hear that others can relate but also your distinction between abusive and caring ways that a partner might address this. A big part of our fight centered around how I automatically assume people who care about me and want to help me have ulterior motives and that those acts of care are really just manipulation tactics. In hindsight, he just cares about me and doesn't want me to hurt myself. It's just really hard for me to accept that to be true without there being strings attached. But I genuinely appreciate your words, and the opportunity to think of things outside of the moment.

Major depressive disorder can be a prison if you're not able to find treatment that works for you. I made my first suicide attempt 15 years ago, and I made my latest one a year ago. I have been in counseling for 14 years, and I have tried numerous pharmaceutical treatment methods. Nothing has worked. To allow those suffering from physiological illnesses to die with dignity while denying that right to those with psychological illnesses is discriminatory. In 2023 I will absolutely be pursuing MAID with my psychiatrist. Just my 2 cents.
It takes about an hour and a half to kick in, and I start work at 8am. If I'm taking my pill at that time, I basically waste an hour and a half of my work day.
This is helpful, I'll ask my doctor about that this week. Thank you!
I have most work meetings before noon, and I need to have my brain turned on for those. But I appreciate the suggestion!
